Bears and lions spare lions. The person who has obtained leadership over all these things, being prudent and reasoning about each thing, does not perceive having fallen into extreme foolishness. For the unwise person considers courage to be a notion of being fearless; and looking at savagery as a glorious reputation; not honoring common nature, not honoring the creator, not considering anything that contributes to sober reasoning; but being uneducated and boastful about things that should bring shame, so that Paul justly says: 'Their glory is in their shame.' The blessed prophet, marveling, says: 'Did not one God create us? Is there not one Father of all of us? Why does each of you abandon your brother?' For all who inhabit this surrounding world, having come from one father, are found to be of one origin. For there is one leader of our race, Adam; and one God created us; not so that we may divide and separate from each other, but so that, having sprung from one root and being bound by natural ties of love, we may reject unnatural madness and make fratricidal anger foreign to our minds. And we say these things especially to you, who inhabit the land of the Egyptians. For spiritual fathers should not have allowed you to be untaught, but should have guided you as children towards what is beneficial and a lawful civic life.

Frightful things are reported to us, that some of you dare to do the most shameful and difficult things, and young men, having become confident in their bodily strength, and misusing the needs of their youth, arm their right hands with a sword, and are taught to wield a club, more savagely than the law of their local custom allows, and they spend the prime of their life in unholy pursuits, either gathering pretexts for anger against their neighbors, and attacking them irrationally, or loving the forgiveness of other people's money, and not perceiving themselves to be entangling themselves in unbreakable snares, and subjecting themselves to death and bitter dangers, for it is written that transgressions hunt down a man, and each one is bound by the chains of their own sins, but, my children, according to Paul, I testify to you with a loud voice, instructing the disorderly, and guiding those who are still reckless in their youth, to stop such transgressions, and to cease causing pain and provoking the King and Lord of all, and to cast away the murderous sword from your hand, and the unjust desire for other people's things from your mind, and to restrain your impulses towards each other, and to calm your anger, and to stop your unholy endeavors

Do not look at Cain, the brother-killer, the unfeeling one, the teacher of impiety in bloodshed. But the Creator of all said to him: 'The voice of your brother's blood cries out to me from the earth.' This word extends to all who are like him. For each of those who dare such things should hear, and now God's voice cries out no less: 'The voice of your brother's blood cries out to me from the earth.' Just as it was said to him again: 'You will be groaning and trembling on the earth,' so also God, the God of love, will say again to each of those who are like him. For what is more cowardly than the one who transgresses the law? What word does not terrify him? What does not make him shudder, even if he just looks at himself? For his conscience always falls within and is convicted by the accusations of sin. The righteous one, indeed, trusts like a lion, and with a free conscience, he is a witness to every good work and is fearless of every accusation. But the one who loves sin, his conscience is weakened to cowardice. Therefore, let us say, as the prophetic word says: 'Awake, you drunkards, from your wine…'

Mourn, all who drink wine to intoxication, for joy and cheer have been taken away from your mouth. The true word of experience is seen in us. What kind of story do the Egyptian farmers have for us now? What kind of word brings joy and cheer? Who among you, whether small or great, has not been affected by the recently inflicted wrath, falling into insensitivity, so as to be able to stop lamenting and wailing, and not show a tear-stained face? The prophet's words are aptly spoken about us now. The farmers mourn over the wheat and barley, for the harvest has perished from the field. The vine has dried up, and the fig trees have failed. The pomegranate, palm, apple, and all the trees of the field have dried up, because the sons of men have been put to shame. For God, who is good and merciful by nature, has shown us a fruitful earth, but the inhabitants of the earth have been put to shame. The hills of the stately trees were once high, nourishing the hopes of the weary and filling the farmer's soul with courage. But the inhabitants of the earth have been put to shame, for they have turned to bloodshed and have drunk the earth with human blood, lifting the sword of brotherly hatred against each other, and thus have become workers of extreme impiety. Our loving God has been justly angered.

and with fire he fortified the fruit-bearing earth, and as with a bridle he turned the expected passions into lamentation, changing joy into sorrow. And this was said by one of the holy prophets: 'Thus says the Lord God Almighty: In all streets there is lamentation, and in all roads it will be said: Woe, woe; a farmer will be called to mourning and lamentation, and those who know mourning, in all roads there is lamentation, because I will pass through the midst,' said the Lord. But see how true the word is. For would not someone say that the events that have occurred are worthy of lamentation and endless mourning? Behold, the bitter beast of famine is devouring our entire land; and the food that is under the sun, so to speak, needs the bread that is thrown to it, and the food that is not very suitable for humans, so that even the prophet Jeremiah may justly lament over it, saying: 'All her people are groaning, seeking bread.' And again: 'The tongue of the suckling child has cleaved to its palate due to thirst. Infants have asked for bread, and there was no one to break it for them. Those who ate delicacies have been reduced to poverty in the streets.' - 'For we have tried many things and brought in few,' as it is written, because we have provoked the Spirit of the Lord. Therefore, I will repent, and concerning the ancient things...
pass_b_english: Bears and lions, despite their ferocity, spare their own kind, but humans, who have been entrusted with leadership over all creation, often fail to recognize their own foolishness. This is because they mistakenly believe that courage is about being fearless, and that savagery is something to be proud of. They do not honor their common human nature, nor do they reverence the Creator who made them, nor do they consider anything else that contributes to sober reasoning. Instead, they boast shamelessly about things that should bring shame, so that Paul justly says: 'Their glory is in their shame' (Phil 3:19).

The prophet, in his wisdom, marvels at this state of affairs and asks, 'Did not one God create us? Is there not one Father of us all?' (Gen 2:24; Mal 2:10). He laments the fact that humans abandon their brothers and sisters, despite being of one origin. For just as there is one leader of the human race, Adam, and one God who created us, so too should we recognize our shared humanity and strive for unity, rather than division and strife. We should be bound together by natural ties of love and reject the unnatural madness that leads to fratricidal anger. This is the message that we bring to you, especially to those of you who inhabit the land of the Egyptians. Spiritual fathers should guide their children towards what is beneficial and a lawful civic life, rather than leaving them to be untaught and ignorant.

Frightful things are being reported to us, and it is said that some of you are daring to do the most shameful and difficult things. Young men, having become confident in their bodily strength, are misusing the needs of their youth and arming themselves with swords, and they are being taught to wield clubs more savagely than the law of their local custom allows.

They spend the prime of their life in unholy pursuits, either gathering pretexts for anger against their neighbors and attacking them irrationally, or loving the forgiveness of other people's money and not perceiving themselves to be entangling themselves in unbreakable snares, and subjecting themselves to death and bitter dangers. For it is written that transgressions hunt down a man, and each one is bound by the chains of their own sins (Prov 5:22).

But, my children, according to Paul, I testify to you with a loud voice, instructing the disorderly and guiding those who are still reckless in their youth, to stop such transgressions and to cease causing pain and provoking the King and Lord of all. You must cast away the murderous sword from your hand and the unjust desire for other people's things from your mind, and restrain your impulses towards each other, and calm your anger, and stop your unholy endeavors.

We must not look to Cain, the brother-killer, as an example. He was unfeeling and taught impiety through his violent actions. However, the Creator of all things spoke to him, saying, 'The voice of your brother's blood cries out to me from the earth' (Gen 4:10). This warning extends to all who would follow in his footsteps. Each person who dares to commit such atrocities should hear God's voice, which cries out no less today: 'The voice of your brother's blood cries out to me from the earth.' Just as it was told to him again, 'You will be groaning and trembling on the earth' (Gen 3:17), so too will God say to each of those who commit similar evils.

The one who transgresses the law is cowardly, and what word does not terrify him? Even a glance at himself is enough to make him shudder. For his conscience always falls within, convicted by the accusations of sin. On the other hand, the righteous one trusts like a lion and is a witness to every good work, fearless of every accusation. But the one who loves sin is weakened to cowardice. Therefore, let us heed the prophetic word, which says, 'Awake, you drunkards, from your wine…' (Amos 8:8).

All who indulge in excessive wine consumption are called to mourn, for the joy and cheer that once filled their lives have been taken away. The true word of experience is evident in our current situation, and it is a stark reminder of the consequences of our actions. The Egyptian farmers, who were once renowned for their fertile land, now have a tale of woe to tell. What kind of story can they share with us, and what kind of word can bring us joy and cheer in these desperate times? It seems that no one, regardless of their social status, has been spared from the devastating effects of the recently inflicted wrath. The prophet's words, which speak of the withering of the vine, the failure of the fig trees, and the drying up of the pomegranate, palm, and apple trees, are a poignant reminder of the desolation that has befallen us (Amos 8:23).

The good and merciful God, who is the giver of all good things, had provided us with a fruitful earth, but the inhabitants of the earth have been put to shame. The hills, which were once adorned with stately trees, now stand as a testament to the transience of human hopes and the fleeting nature of courage. The earth, which was once nourished by the blood of the righteous, has been drunk with human blood, and the sword of brotherly hatred has been lifted against each other. As a result, God has been justly angered, and we are left to mourn the loss of our joy and cheer.

The earth, which was once fruitful, has been fortified with fire, and the passions that were expected have been turned into lamentation, changing joy into sorrow. The prophet's words have come true, as we see the devastating effects of famine in our land. The food that was once abundant is now scarce, and the people are groaning with hunger, seeking bread.

The prophet Jeremiah lamented over the situation, saying that all the people are groaning, seeking bread (Jer 8:20), and that even the infants are suffering from thirst. The tongue of the suckling child has cleaved to its palate due to thirst, and there is no one to break bread for them. Those who once ate delicacies are now reduced to poverty in the streets. We have tried many things, but our efforts have been in vain, and we have provoked the Spirit of the Lord. Therefore, I will repent and reflect on the ancient things...
